title: Introduce CompactionResult contract and compact boundaries
objective: Replace the Go compactor's raw []Message return contract with a TypeScript-equivalent CompactionResult model and compact boundary semantics.
implementation_scope: Define a Go CompactionResult struct with boundary marker, summary messages, attachments, hook results, optional messages-to-keep, display text, token counts, and usage fields.
Add compact boundary message representation carrying trigger, pre-compact token count, previous tail identifier, pre-compact discovered tool names, and preserved segment metadata.
Add BuildPostCompactMessages(result) and GetMessagesAfterCompactBoundary(messages) helpers matching the TS order: boundary, summary, messagesToKeep, attachments, hookResults.
Update the Compactor interface and current SummaryCompactor callers to use CompactionResult or a clearly named adapter while preserving existing public engine behavior.
Ensure existing simple compaction tests are updated to assert boundary and summary placement.
out_of_scope: Do not implement auto-compact orchestration in this task.
Do not implement post-compact attachment recovery beyond fitting the new contract around the current file recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All compaction paths can construct post-compact messages through one shared BuildPostCompactMessages helper.
Repeated compaction only summarizes messages after the latest compact boundary.
The old []Message-only contract is no longer the primary internal compact API.
Tests cover full compact, no-op compact, repeated compact, and preserved tail ordering.
risks: Changing the compactor interface affects query loop, engine, and command call sites.
Boundary messages must not be sent to providers in an invalid role/content shape.
dispatch_prompt: Implement the CompactionResult and compact boundary foundation for Go context compaction, keeping behavior compatible with current callers while exposing the richer TS-like contract.
